The arrival in North Africa of the Moriscos, the Muslims of Spain who had been forced to become Christians, after Philip III ordered them out of Spain between 1609 and 1614.

About 300,000 people were shipped out, many from Valencia and Aragon. This was the last chapter of the long end of al-Andalus. Most landed in Morocco, around Algiers and Oran, and in Tunisia. The crossing and the first years were hard; some were robbed or killed on arrival, and some had spoken only Spanish.

Many still made new homes. In Tunisia the ruler welcomed them, and they founded or rebuilt towns such as Testour, with Andalusian building styles and crafts. In Morocco, refugees from Hornachos and others set up the Republic of Salé, a corsair base that raided Spanish and other Christian shipping and joined the wider world of the Barbary corsairs.

Andalusian music, cooking, family names and building traditions in the cities of the Maghreb still trace back to these refugees and earlier ones. The Spanish side of the story is the expulsion itself.
sum: The arrival in North Africa of the Moriscos, the Muslims of Spain who had been forced to become Christians, after Philip III ordered them out of Spain between 1609 and 1614.
